# Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta (MN 45 (PTS MN i 305))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta* ("The Shorter Discourse on Taking Up Practices", MN 45) is the forty-fifth discourse of the Majjhimanikāya, located at PTS MN i 305 [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Set in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove in Anāthapiṇḍika's Park, the discourse presents the Buddha instructing the bhikkhus on four ways of undertaking practices or actions (*dhamma-samādāna*), categorized by whether they are pleasant or painful in the present and whether they result in pleasant or painful fruit in the future: (1) pleasant now but ripening in future pain, (2) painful now and ripening in future pain, (3) painful now but ripening in future pleasure, and (4) pleasant now and ripening in future pleasure [Piya Tan 2002; Farrington; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003].
In expounding the first category, the Buddha addresses the view held by certain ascetics and brahmins who assert that there is no danger or harm in sensual pleasures (*natthi kāmesu doso*) [Jayatilleke 1963]. The insidious nature of indulgence and habit formation is illustrated by the memorable Simile of the Creeper, showing how subtle attachments and detrimental tendencies grow strong if left unchecked [SuttaCentral; Nyanaponika 1986]. The discourse also surveys various harsh ascetic practices and mistaken paths that yield suffering both now and in the future [Piya Tan 2002; Farrington; Hazra 1994].
According to SuttaCentral, full parallels to MN 45 include MĀ 174 in the Chinese Madhyama Āgama, as well as DN 8 (*Mahāsīhanāda Sutta*), DN 25 (*Udumbarika Sutta*), MN 12 (*Mahāsīhanāda Sutta*), MN 51 (*Kandaraka Sutta*), MN 60 (*Apaṇṇaka Sutta*), AN 3.156–162, and AN 4.198; the text is also cited or mentioned in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 15) and *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms extensive Pali text reuse with its companion discourse MN 46 (*Mahādhammasamādāna Sutta*), as well as AN 4 (AN 4.198), AN 3 (AN 3.156–162), MN 51, DN 8, Pp 2.4, and MN 12 [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with the Chinese Madhyama Āgama (T26) [DharmaNexus].
